active_projects.title: Close the two measured curated-array coverage gaps in the agent-contract lint: normalize the books agents Check C/G bullets, and rule on bounded-wait scope for the twenty-three research agents
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS. No task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md); they are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

GOAL. lint-agent-contracts.sh asserts contract-bullet coverage against CURATED path arrays, one per check. Two gaps in those arrays are now measured, not suspected. Close both, and in doing so rule on whether the curated-array shape is the right mechanism at all or whether it structurally invites this drift.

Both gaps are the same mechanism on the same two scripts (lint-agent-contracts.sh and its test file), which is why they are one task rather than two: splitting them would force a serializing dependency between two tasks editing the same two files, for no gain.

=== GAP 1: THE BOOKS AGENTS ARE ABSENT FROM CHECK C AND CHECK G ===

MEASURED 2026-10-07 by direct re-derivation against the lint's own expected text (the fragment lines it greps for), not carried from a prior record:

  books/agents/books-implementation-agent.md       C=MISS G=MISS
  books/agents/books-implementation-hard-agent.md  C=MISS G=MISS

Neither file appears in Check C's IN_SCOPE_RELATIVE_PATHS (32 lines) nor Check G's OWNERSHIP_IN_SCOPE_RELATIVE_PATHS (16 lines). Both DO appear in the newly added Check H's BOUNDED_WAIT_IN_SCOPE_RELATIVE_PATHS and both PASS it.

A PRIOR RECORD STATES THIS GAP INCORRECTLY. The bounded-wait propagation task's summary records this as a pure curated-list omission, asserting both files "carry the no-task-references bullet (confirmed by direct grep)". That assertion does not survive re-derivation and the correction changes the fix:

  - books-implementation-agent.md item 6 carries the canonical Check C wording but LINE-WRAPPED across two lines ("-- see\n   `.claude/rules/...`"). The lint greps a single line with grep -qF, so a wrapped bullet cannot match however correct its prose.
  - books-implementation-hard-agent.md item 7 is an ABBREVIATED PARAPHRASE ("Reference task numbers in files outside `specs/**`") missing both the ("task N", "tasks N-M") parenthetical and the rule cross-reference.
  - Check G's bullet is absent from both as a bullet. books-implementation-agent.md discusses `**Status**:` ownership in prose (around lines 100-101 and 126-127) but not as the canonical MUST-NOT line.

CONSEQUENCE: adding the two paths to the C and G arrays WITHOUT first normalizing the bullet text makes the lint FAIL. Normalize first, then register. Do not trust the prior summary's framing; the measurement above is the baseline.

RULE ON THE LINE-WRAP CASE SPECIFICALLY. A single-line grep -qF against a hand-wrapped markdown bullet is brittle by construction: a correct contract fails the check purely on line breaks. Decide whether the checks should normalize whitespace before comparing (making wrapped-but-correct bullets pass) or whether the fragment bullets must be held unwrapped by convention. Whichever is chosen, state it where a future bullet author will see it, and pin it with a fixture.

=== GAP 2: ALL TWENTY-THREE RESEARCH AGENTS LACK THE BOUNDED-WAIT BULLET PAIR ===

MEASURED 2026-10-07 across every *research*agent*.md in the source store, against the two canonical fragment lines Check H greps: covered=0, missing=23.

  books/agents/books-research-agent.md, books/agents/books-research-hard-agent.md,
  core/agents/general-research-agent.md, cslib/agents/cslib-research-agent.md,
  cslib/agents/cslib-research-hard-agent.md, cslib/agents/pr-review-research-agent.md,
  epidemiology/agents/epi-research-agent.md, formal/agents/formal-research-agent.md,
  formal/agents/logic-research-agent.md, formal/agents/math-research-agent.md,
  formal/agents/physics-research-agent.md, founder/agents/deck-research-agent.md,
  latex/agents/latex-research-agent.md, lean/agents/lean-research-agent.md,
  lean/agents/lean-research-hard-agent.md, nix/agents/nix-research-agent.md,
  nvim/agents/neovim-research-agent.md, present/agents/slides-research-agent.md,
  python/agents/python-research-agent.md, rust/agents/rust-research-agent.md,
  typst/agents/typst-research-agent.md, web/agents/web-research-agent.md,
  z3/agents/z3-research-agent.md

The bounded-wait propagation task deliberately scoped research agents OUT, recording the reason in the fragment itself: its measured evidence and acceptance surface were implementation-agent-only. It recommended this follow-up reusing the identical mechanism. Two specifics it recorded and this task must honour or refute:

  - general-research-agent.md already carries the REMOTE-wait half of the discipline but not the local-build half -- the same partial-coverage shape that motivated the original propagation.
  - The Lean research agents' run_in_background hits are a SEPARATE SANCTIONED build-guard path, not instances of the defect. Do not count them as coverage and do not break them.

DO NOT ASSUME ALL 23 ARE IN SCOPE. The bullet forbids backgrounding a LOCAL verification/gate/build/test process. A research agent with no Bash access, or one that never runs a local build, is not exposed and a bullet it cannot violate is noise. Determine which subset genuinely holds the exposure (frontmatter tool grants plus actual local-build invocation), and record the excluded files WITH THEIR REASON the way the implementation-agent fragment already records its own exclusions. active_projects.title: Teach the non-destructive history-read techniques at the point of use, so an implementation agent inspecting past file state never reverts a shared working tree

SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS. GOAL. Teach the non-destructive history-read techniques AT THE POINT OF USE, so an implementation agent that needs to inspect historical file state reaches for a read-only technique instead of reverting a shared working tree.

=== WHY THIS IS A MISSING-INSTRUCTION SIGNAL, NOT TWO COINCIDENCES ===

2026-10-07, Logos/Verification, one /orchestrate batch of four tasks sharing one working tree. TWO implementation agents INDEPENDENTLY reached for the same wrong tool (bare whole-tree `git stash`) for the same CORRECT need: isolating a pre-existing test failure from their own edit. Independent convergence on one wrong tool by two agents is a missing-instruction signal.

THE RIGHT TECHNIQUES ALREADY EXIST AND WERE USED ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME BATCH -- which is what proves the gap is discoverability, not capability:
  - One planner used a DETACHED WORKTREE for a read-only historical inspection, successfully.
  - One implementation agent recovered its OWN lost edit safely, via a read-only `git show <stash-ref>:path` extraction.
Nothing teaches either technique where an IMPLEMENTATION AGENT would look. The knowledge was in the system and still did not reach the two agents who needed it.

RE-DERIVE THESE BEFORE RELYING ON THEM. The two-agent count, the detached-worktree planner instance, and the `git show <stash-ref>:path` recovery instance are carried figures in this description. Re-confirm them and report any divergence.

=== DECIDED CONTEXT -- DO NOT REOPEN ===

The user has ruled OUT per-agent worktree isolation for parallel dispatch, consistent with the existing decision record specs/decisions/worktree-isolation-removal-reaffirmation.md and the confirmed re-argued verdict recorded in the measured-co-scheduling-signal task's NON-GOALS. PARALLEL DISPATCHES WILL CONTINUE TO SHARE ONE WORKING TREE AS A DELIBERATE CHOICE.

Therefore the only defences against cross-task interference are:
  (a) declared file_scope disjointness at admission,
  (b) dependencies[] edges for ordering,
  (c) AGENT-SIDE DISCIPLINE about tree-wide operations.
THIS TASK SUPPLIES (c). Do NOT propose, re-rule on, or defer a question about worktree isolation. A deliverable that reopens it is out of scope.

=== SCOPE ===

Author a SHORT shared-worktree discipline section stating:
  - Read history with `git show HEAD:path` or `git show <ref>:path`; read differences with `git diff HEAD -- path`.
  - Copy to a scratchpad for experiments that need a mutable file.
  - NEVER `git stash`, `git checkout -- <path>`, or `git restore <path>` on a shared tree -- these revert the tree out from under concurrent writers.
It must be REACHABLE FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION AGENT DEFINITIONS, not merely filed somewhere correct. A section nobody's context path reaches is the same failure this task exists to fix.

DETACHED WORKTREE: it MAY be mentioned, but it MUST be explicitly labelled a READ-ONLY INSPECTION TECHNIQUE and never an isolation strategy, so no reader can take it as reopening the settled question above.

THE CHOICE: this task DECLARES A DEPENDENCY on the bounded-wait propagation task (dependencies: [356]) rather than confining itself to the shared standards file. Serializing behind it gets both the shared section AND a live pointer, with no concurrent edit to the fourteen definitions. active_projects.title: Post-incident verification checklist for destructive git on a shared tree, naming uncommitted pre-session tree state as the first mandatory check
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/ (never .claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS. No task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md): cite by filename, command or concept. Task numbers are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

GOAL. A one-page post-incident verification checklist for an agent that has just taken a destructive or tree-wide git action on a shared working tree, naming UNCOMMITTED PRE-SESSION TREE STATE as the FIRST mandatory check.

=== THE FAILURE WAS VERIFICATION SCOPE, NOT CANDOUR -- WHICH IS WHY A CHECKLIST FIXES IT ===

2026-10-07, Logos/Verification, one /orchestrate batch sharing one working tree. Two implementation agents each ran a bare whole-tree `git stash`; one stash spanned a long build and its `git stash pop` aborted, applying nothing.

DISCLOSURE QUALITY IN BOTH INCIDENTS WAS GENUINELY HIGH. Both agents self-reported PROMPTLY and UNPROMPTED, with accurate accounts of what they had done. Nothing was concealed. The defect was entirely in WHAT THEY CHECKED:
  - Both checked (i) sibling COMMITS and (ii) their own edits.
  - Both found those intact.
  - Both therefore concluded "no sibling content lost".
  - THE ONLY ACTUAL LOSS sat in PRE-EXISTING UNCOMMITTED TREE STATE that neither thought to check -- roughly thirty files of the user's pre-session work, surviving only inside a 53-file stash entry.
  - The orchestrator found it only by DIFFING THE WORKING TREE AGAINST THE STASH ENTRY.

Because candour was already high, no amount of additional disclosure pressure would have caught this. A checklist that names the missing category will.

=== THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES THIS DECEPTIVE (and the reason for the ordering below) ===

A REVERTED FILE MATCHES HEAD. So it reads as CLEAN to `git status`, to `git diff`, and to every naive check. ABSENCE OF A MODIFICATION IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE OF A PROBLEM unless you compare against the stash entry or the reflog. This is why "I checked git status and it was clean" is not evidence of no loss, and why the checklist must say so explicitly rather than merely listing checks.

RE-DERIVE THESE BEFORE RELYING ON THEM. The ~30 files, the 53-file stash entry, the two-agent count, and the aborted-pop mechanism are carried figures in this description. Re-confirm them and report any divergence.

=== SCOPE ===

ONE PAGE. A CHECKLIST, NOT A FRAMEWORK. It names, as MANDATORY checks IN THIS ORDER:

  (1) PRE-SESSION UNCOMMITTED TRACKED MODIFICATIONS -- compared against THE STASH ENTRY and THE REFLOG, NOT merely against HEAD. State the concrete commands.
  (2) UNTRACKED FILES.
  (3) SIBLING COMMITS.
  (4) THE AGENT'S OWN EDITS.

UNCOMMITTED STATE GOES FIRST, and the checklist must say WHY: it is the ONLY category with NO OTHER RECOVERY PATH. A sibling commit survives in history; an agent's own edit can be redone; pre-session uncommitted work exists in exactly one place and, once reverted, reads as clean. Ordering by recoverability, not by convenience, is the substance of this deliverable -- a checklist with the same four items in a different order would reproduce the original failure.

PAIR WITH THE STASH-RECLASSIFICATION TASK: that task's guard refusal message should be able to POINT AT this checklist. Add that cross-reference HERE, against the finished refusal text -- which is why this task is serialized behind it (dependencies: [361]) and declares the guard hook in its file_scope. Do not edit the guard's patterns, classes, or rule text; add the pointer only.

Prefer a new one-page file under `context/standards/` (survey `git-safety.md`, `git-staging-scope.md`, and `git-workflow-narrative.md` first and record the rejected placements). If it fits as a section of an existing standards document without burying it, that is preferable to a new file -- but a checklist that must be findable UNDER INCIDENT CONDITIONS argues for its own named page; rule on this and say why.

=== EXPLICIT NON-GOALS ===

- Do NOT build an incident-management framework, a severity taxonomy, or a reporting template. One page, four ordered checks.
- Do NOT add disclosure or candour requirements. Disclosure was already high; that is not the defect.
- Do NOT change the guard's patterns, DESTRUCTIVE_ACTION_CLASS values, escape hatch, or the git-workflow rule text -- the stash-reclassification task owns all of those. Pointer only.
- Do NOT retroactively audit past incidents in any repo. Forward-looking checklist only.
- Do NOT propose worktree isolation; it is ruled out (specs/decisions/worktree-isolation-removal-reaffirmation.md).
- Do NOT hand-edit any deployed `.claude/**` copy.

=== FILE_SCOPE OVERLAPS WITH OPEN TASKS ===

Declared overlap with the stash-reclassification task on `hooks/guard-destructive-git.sh`, resolved by the dependency edge: this task runs after, and touches only the refusal message's cross-reference line.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

- A one-page checklist exists with the four checks in the stated order.
- Check (1) names concrete stash-entry and reflog comparison commands, not just "check uncommitted state".
- The checklist states explicitly that a reverted file matches HEAD and therefore reads as clean, so a clean `git status` is not evidence of no loss.
- The ordering rationale (uncommitted state first because it has no other recovery path) is stated in the deliverable, not just in this description.
- The guard's refusal message points at the checklist, and the guard's patterns/classes/escape hatch are otherwise unchanged.
- Length is one page; placement decision and rejected alternatives recorded.
- No task-number references in any deliverable outside specs/**.

active_projects.title: Suite-level selection within Gate 8: --filter/--only in run-all.sh plus the touched-file-to-suite mapping
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never .claude/**, a disposable
deploy artifact), per rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md.

== OWNER FRAMING (carries across this three-task batch) ==

These enhancements must apply WIDELY: improve the planning skills, context, templates and agent
definitions as appropriate so the system tests efficiently WHERE IT COUNTS, rather than bogging
down development with redundant testing. This is a planning-layer change, not a one-off flag on
one script. This task is the MECHANISM half; the tier-selection-discipline task is the GUIDANCE
half and depends on this one so its guidance can cite the flag introduced here.

== THE GAP, LOCATED PRECISELY ==

verify-deploy.sh --only-gate N,M already provides GATE-level selection. Selection WITHIN Gate 8
does not exist: scripts/tests/run-all.sh has no --filter and no --only (verified by grep, zero
matches). Its entire flag surface is run-all.sh:34 (usage) and the parse loop at run-all.sh:127-144
-- exactly --quiet, --timings FILE, --jobs N|auto, --fail-on-new. So a task touching five files
runs all 92 suites or none.

Gate 8 is the dominant cost. verify-deploy.sh is 20 gates; Gate 8 (verify-deploy.sh:566-596, the
invocation itself at :591) is 92 suites / 44,682 lines of test code and roughly 70% of a full
run's wall clock. On an idle host a full run is ~2.8 min. On a LOADED host with several concurrent
agent sessions -- the owner's normal operating condition --
context/standards/shell-script-testing.md records 14m1.5s sequential and 6m47.4s under --jobs auto.

== WHY THIS IS THE LIVE HALF OF AN ALREADY-DIAGNOSED PROBLEM ==

context/standards/shell-script-testing.md already records the core finding verbatim: the
orchestrator's redeploy checkpoints "were found to re-run the full shell-test battery 2-3 times per
cycle ON TOP OF every dispatched implementation agent's own phase-gate run of the identical battery
against the identical source-store tree -- a measured, dominant wall-clock cost, not additional
coverage".

The --skip-slow remedy was applied to the ORCHESTRATOR checkpoints ONLY
(scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh:942, scripts/command-gate-out.sh:208, scripts/deploy-headless.sh).
The AGENT-SIDE phase-gate re-run named in that same sentence was identified and LEFT IN PLACE.
That is the live gap, and it cannot be closed by --skip-slow: an agent's mid-task phase gate needs
REAL coverage of what the phase touched, not a skip. It needs SELECTION. Supplying that selection
is this task's whole purpose.

== THE WORK ==

(1) Add subset selection to run-all.sh. Settle the flag name and surface (--filter PATTERN vs
--only SUITE[,SUITE] vs both) rather than assuming; --only-gate already sets a naming precedent in
verify-deploy.sh worth matching or deliberately departing from.

(2) Build the mechanical touched-file -> suite mapping. The naming convention already supports it:
guard-destructive-git.sh <-> test-guard-destructive-git.sh, lint-NAME.sh <-> test-lint-NAME.sh. Give
the mapping a durable home of its own (scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh is the declared candidate)
so both run-all.sh and a future caller consume one implementation rather than two drifting copies.

(3) The mapping MUST report what it could not map. A touched file with no derivable suite is the
dangerous case: silently selecting zero suites would read as green. Decide and record the fail-safe
direction (the house direction is fail-SAFE -- an unmapped touched file escalates to the full sweep
rather than selecting nothing) and prove it with a test.

== LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT: DEPLOYED-VS-SOURCE SUBJECT RESOLUTION ==

A recorded measurement from the completed Gate 8 parallelization work states that 41 of 73 files
then under scripts/tests/ prefer the DEPLOYED copy of their subject-under-test over the
source-store copy. RE-MEASURE that ratio against today's 92 suites rather than carrying the old
figure. It matters here because a source-store path is the mapping's INPUT while a deployed path may
be the suite's actual subject -- a naive basename mapping can select a suite that is not in fact
exercising the edited file. Do not design the mapping without resolving this.

== MUST COMPOSE, NOT BYPASS ==

Selection must compose with the existing machinery, all of it already load-bearing in run-all.sh:
  - --jobs and its JOBS_CAP=4 plus the auto resolution (run-all.sh:156-167)
  - the nested-invocation guard that forces JOBS=1 (run-all.sh:173)
  - the separate sequential path kept deliberately byte-identical (run-all.sh:283-285) and the
    parallel path (run-all.sh:325)
  - LOAD_SENSITIVE_BASENAMES, which always runs alone and serially before the pool
    (run-all.sh:353-364, indices at :380-384)
  - the TOTAL_ACCOUNTED reconciliation (run-all.sh:429), which a selection pass must keep honest
  - known-failures.txt and the EXPECTED/NEW classification (run-all.sh:260-264, :518-540)
  - --timings
Settled decision 13 (specs/ROADMAP.md) binds here: known-failures.txt is advisory and "never
changes which suites run". Selection is therefore a strictly separate axis from it, and the two must
not be conflated.

== MUST PRESERVE ==

The full sweep still runs at the final gate. context/formats/plan-format.md:273-277 states the
non-negotiable invariant -- tiering governs GRANULARITY ONLY and a scheme that weakens the final
gate "is wrong, not a trade-off". Nothing here may make Gate 8's own full invocation
(verify-deploy.sh:591) narrower by default; selection is strictly OPT-IN at the call site.

Settled decision 15 (specs/ROADMAP.md) also binds: Gate 8's deployed-tree coverage is knowingly
reduced under --skip-slow, so a --skip-slow pass is NOT evidence that doc-sync pins hold. A selected
subset pass is likewise not such evidence, and must not be presented as one.

== DO NOT RE-PROPOSE (rejected alternatives recorded in run-all.sh's own header, with measurements) ==

  - raising the --jobs cap above 4: suites rsync a ~16MB fixture tree or launch headless nvim, so N
    concurrent copies blow past per-suite sizing
  - a self-maintaining timing cache: mutable tree state, with gitignore and deploy-hygiene
    consequences
  - line count as a cost proxy: disproven, a 261-line suite cost ~391s while a 3,839-line suite
    cost ~45s

== FILE_SCOPE EXCLUSIONS, DELIBERATE AND REASONED ==

Two files this task will touch are deliberately absent from file_scope under ROADMAP Settled
decision 17 carve-out (b) (breadth: "a coarse shared path (a manifest, a root gate script, a
directory-root scope) ... narrow the file_scope instead" of demanding an edge):

  - agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json -- the new test suite needs a one-line registration
    in the tests/test-*.sh array (manifest.json:188 onward, 92 entries today). A manifest is the
    named carve-out case and is claimed by six open tasks. Make the one-line addition; do not
    declare it.
  - agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/verify-deploy.sh -- a root gate script, claimed by two
    open tasks. It is excluded because this task does NOT need it: Gate 8 keeps running the full
    sweep unchanged, which is the MUST PRESERVE invariant above, and a cheaper tier invokes
    run-all.sh with the new selection flag directly. If research concludes a verify-deploy.sh
    pass-through is genuinely required, record it as a FOLLOW-UP rather than widening scope here.

== SERIALIZING EDGES ADDED TO DOWNSTREAM TASKS (not to this one) ==

Per Settled decision 17, an overlap is resolved by adding an edge, not by separating the pair. Two
edges were added pointing AT this task rather than from it, because this task is a narrow
single-flag enabler while both others are broad corpus refactors that benefit from selection
already existing:

  - 170 (isolate_shell_suites_from_host_state) owns
    context/standards/shell-script-testing.md, this task's one contended path. Edge: 170 depends on
    this task.
  - 328 (systematic_script_and_test_corpus_efficiency) declares no file_scope but its own text
    claims this exact ground -- "(b) The 85 test suites: cut per-suite startup cost and the Gate 8
    117.9s figure" -- and it is the standing consumer of script-inventory.sh per Settled decision 16.
    Edge: 328 depends on this task.

== ACCEPTANCE: DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED ==

  1. A MEASURED before/after wall-clock figure for a representative selected subset versus the full
     sweep, both on the same host, with the host's concurrent-session load stated. A figure without
     its load condition is not a result, given the 2.8min-vs-14min idle/loaded spread.
  2. The pass/fail set of a selected run is a strict SUBSET of the full run's, with no suite
     reporting differently under selection than without it.
  3. An unmapped touched file demonstrably triggers the recorded fail-safe direction, proven by a
     test, not by inspection.
  4. --jobs, the nested guard, LOAD_SENSITIVE_BASENAMES serialization, TOTAL_ACCOUNTED,
     known-failures.txt classification and --timings all behave identically with and without
     selection.
  5. With no selection flag passed, run-all.sh output is byte-identical to today's.
  6. scripts/tests/ passes. No suite may be weakened, skipped or deleted to make this land.

active_projects.title: Reduce the deploy-staleness completion round trip without weakening the completion-deploy gate
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never .claude/**, a disposable
deploy artifact), per rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md.

== OWNER FRAMING (carries across this three-task batch) ==

These enhancements must apply WIDELY: improve the planning skills, context, templates and agent
definitions as appropriate so the system tests efficiently WHERE IT COUNTS, rather than bogging
down development with redundant testing. This is a planning-layer change, not a one-off flag on one
script. This task is the batch's third cost surface: not redundant testing, but a redundant CYCLE
spent re-deploying so an already-finished task can record its own completion.

== THE OBSERVED COST, WITH ITS THREE MEASURED INSTANCES ==

A task touching agent-system/** reliably finishes its work and then cannot record it. The postflight
completion-deploy gate refuses the status write with exit 6, costing an extra redeploy cycle plus a
reconcile-task-status.sh call. Three instances in a single session (2026-10-07): tasks 356, 358 and
361's first dispatch each completed their work, were refused, and needed the extra cycle to record.
The commit subject "promote stranded completions and stamp plan files" in this repository's history
is the manual remedy being paid by hand. EACH REFUSED CYCLE BURNS A DISPATCH SLOT FROM MAX_CYCLES,
which is the real damage -- the cost is not the deploy, it is the budget.

== THE GATE IS CORRECT. DO NOT WEAKEN IT. ==

The gate prevents recording a completion against a stale deploy, which is a genuine correctness
property. The goal is to remove the WASTED CYCLE, not to soften the refusal. Any design whose effect
is that a completion can be recorded against a stale deployed tree is wrong by construction and must
be rejected in the plan, not traded off.

Gate implementation sites, all verified in the source store 2026-10-07 (READ these; do not
re-derive):
  - scripts/update-task-status.sh:36 documents exit 6; the gate itself is PHASE 0.5, declared
    "unconditional, check-only, exit 6" at :639, exiting at :787. CHECK-ONLY is the key property:
    it refuses and changes nothing.
  - scripts/command-gate-out.sh:180-189 is the rc==6 handler and ALREADY resolves the round trip on
    its own path: it runs "the sanctioned single-task redeploy trigger" inline. The single-task
    /implement path therefore does NOT exhibit this defect.
  - scripts/skill-base.sh:1069-1080 records deploy_pending plus deploy_pending_reason into the
    task's own .return-meta.json.
  - scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1149-1171 is the ORCHESTRATE path, and this is where the
    cost lives: it does NOT redeploy, it DEFERS to the next cycle, and its notice at :1164 promises
    the next cycle's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint "deploys and then automatically reconciles this
    task's status -- no manual action needed unless that deploy or its post-deploy verify fails".

== THE ACTUAL DEFECT: AN EXISTING AUTOMATIC PROMOTION THAT DID NOT FIRE ==

The promised automatic reconcile ALREADY EXISTS. scripts/lib/redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh:51 defines
run_post_deploy_reconcile_pass(), whose own header states it "Makes the checkpoint's own
'convergence is deferred to the next cycle' promise real: promote every task THIS cycle's checkpoint
just deploy-unblocked (post_deploy_reconcile_json, set above inside exactly the three clean-success
branches -- never on branch (a) deploy failure or branch (b) blocking findings) by replaying
reconcile-task-status.sh".

So the mechanism exists, the promise at orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1164 cites it, and yet three
tasks in one session still required a hand-run reconcile. THAT CONTRADICTION IS THE TASK. Research
must establish which of these is true before any fix is designed:
  (a) the promotion pass did not run at all on those cycles;
  (b) it ran but post_deploy_reconcile_json did not include those tasks -- note the header's own
      restriction to "exactly the three clean-success branches", so a deploy with ANY blocking
      finding silently promotes nothing; or
  (c) it ran and promoted, but a later stage overwrote or re-refused the status.
Fixing a cause that was not the cause is the main failure mode available here.

== HARD CONSTRAINT: NO THIRD AUTOMATED DEPLOY-TRIGGER SITE ==

ROADMAP Settled decision 10: the sanctioned automated deploy-trigger count stays at EXACTLY TWO.
The remedy must reuse an existing sanctioned site; it may widen an existing trigger's PREDICATE
(which context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md:165-179 records as explicitly permitted and
already done once -- "only the REACH of its existing trigger predicate changed") but it may not add
a new call site.

A DIVERGENCE TO RESOLVE, NOT INHERIT: the two documents name DIFFERENT pairs.
context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md:171 names "command-gate-out.sh's rc == 6 branch and
commands/implement.md Step 4's batch-refusal trigger". scripts/lib/redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh:13-16
reports that scripts/tests/test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh "enforces, by name, that
deploy-headless.sh has EXACTLY TWO genuine automated callers in the whole corpus --
orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh and command-gate-out.sh". The MECHANICAL source of truth is the lint.
Establish which pair is authoritative and correct the prose; do not add a third site to satisfy
either reading.

ALSO BINDING: redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh:13-32 records that an earlier attempt to move the
deploy-headless.sh call into this library CORRECTLY FAILED test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh, because
a sourced library has no "last physical statement" to wrap and the genuine-caller census then found
three files. That call was deliberately left INLINE in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh. Do not re-attempt
that move, and do not patch the lint to special-case a third shape -- the recorded rule is never
weaken a test to make a refactor pass.

== FILE_SCOPE EXCLUSIONS, DELIBERATE AND REASONED ==

  - scripts/update-task-status.sh is EXCLUDED because the gate is correct and check-only: this task
    must not edit the refusal. (It is also claimed by one open task.)
  - scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh is EXCLUDED. It is the deferral site, and it is claimed
    by five open tasks (273, 284, 304, 335, 350); edging onto all five would park this small fix
    behind the whole group. The remedy is designed to land in the shared promotion library instead,
    so BOTH sanctioned sites inherit it from one change -- which is also the better design under
    Settled decision 10. READ the deferral site; do not edit it. If research proves the fix cannot
    live in the library alone, add the edge then rather than widening scope now.
  - scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh is EXCLUDED for the same contention reason and because the
    inline deploy-headless.sh call there must not be touched (see the lint constraint above).

== ADMISSION GATE, DECLARED HONESTLY ==

scripts/reconcile-task-status.sh IS on context/reference/orchestrator-critical-paths.json (one of
its twelve script entries), so this task DOES trip the self-modification admission gate. Declared
rather than dodged.

== ACCEPTANCE: DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED ==

  1. The cause is NAMED with evidence -- which of (a)/(b)/(c) above actually happened -- before any
     fix is proposed. A fix without an identified cause does not satisfy this task.
  2. A reproduction fixture: a task whose completion write is refused with exit 6, shown recording
     its completion WITHOUT a hand-run reconcile-task-status.sh call. It must fail before the change
     and pass after.
  3. A counted before/after: dispatch cycles consumed from MAX_CYCLES for one agent-system-touching
     task from work-done to status-recorded. The claim of this task is a reduction in that count, so
     that count is the number to report.
  4. The gate still refuses a completion against a genuinely stale deploy -- proven by a test that
     keeps the tree stale and confirms exit 6 and an unchanged state.json.
  5. The sanctioned automated deploy-caller census is still exactly two:
     test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh green, unmodified.
  6. The documented pair in context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md matches what the lint
     mechanically enforces.
  7. scripts/tests/ passes. No suite may be weakened, skipped or deleted to make this land.
  8. shellcheck clean per context/standards/shell-strict-mode.md.

DELIVERABLE RULE: no task-number references in deliverables outside specs/** -- cite file AND line
(the durable anchors used throughout this description), never a task number.

artifacts.summary: Identifies the cause (the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's post-deploy reconcile pass only ever considers tasks named in the current /orchestrate invocation's own task_numbers, never a system-wide scan of specs/state.json), traces the 2026-10-07 incident through git history to confirm it, resolves the regeneration-is-manual-only.md vs. lint sanctioned-site divergence (commands/implement.md no longer exists), and recommends widening run_post_deploy_reconcile_pass() in scripts/lib/redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh to sweep state.json system-wide, with a reproduction fixture plan.
5-phase plan: reproduction harness, system-wide deploy-pending sweep in redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh, acceptance fixture cases, sanctioned-site prose correction, final gate set.

Full acceptance walkthrough (#1-#8), named cause (variant (b), candidate set bounded by .task_numbers), counted before/after, and the two required plan-predicate corrections found during implementation.

active_projects.title: Tier-selection discipline: make a non-final-phase full verification tier justify itself
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never .claude/**, a disposable
deploy artifact), per rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md.

== OWNER FRAMING (carries across this three-task batch) ==

These enhancements must apply WIDELY: improve the planning skills, context, templates and agent
definitions as appropriate so the system tests efficiently WHERE IT COUNTS, rather than bogging down
development with redundant testing. This is a planning-layer change, not a one-off flag on one
script. This task is the GUIDANCE half of the batch: it changes how plans CHOOSE a verification
tier, across the whole planning surface, so plans routinely pick the cheapest tier that actually
covers the phase's blast radius.

== THE MECHANISM EXISTS; SELECTION IS THE PROBLEM ==

context/formats/plan-format.md ALREADY defines the four-tier ladder. Verified anchors:
  - the ordering, prose < local < interface < full, at plan-format.md:258
  - the per-tier table with each tier's declared blind spot at plan-format.md:265-269 (the `full`
    row is :269)
  - the tie-break rule at plan-format.md:271: "When uncertain, apply the strictest applicable tier
    (full > interface > local > prose)"
  - the non-negotiable invariant at plan-format.md:273-277
  - the "a phase declaring `full` names bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh" requirement at
    plan-format.md:279-282

Nothing is missing from the ladder. The defect is that the tie-break at plan-format.md:271 is the
ONLY selection guidance a planner gets, and it biases unconditionally toward `full` -- with no cost
signal anywhere in the surrounding text and no requirement to justify the choice. A planner that
follows the written guidance correctly lands on `full` by default.

== WHAT `full` ACTUALLY COSTS (measured 2026-10-07; USE THIS, DO NOT RE-DERIVE) ==

verify-deploy.sh is 20 gates. Gate 8 (verify-deploy.sh:566-596) is 92 suites / 44,682 lines of test
code and roughly 70% of a full run's wall clock. Idle host: ~2.8 min for a full run. LOADED host
with several concurrent agent sessions -- the owner's normal operating condition --
context/standards/shell-script-testing.md records 14m1.5s sequential and 6m47.4s under --jobs auto.

This cost is multiplied by context/contracts/phase-closure.md:167-169, which requires that a phase's
declared verification "has been run in this dispatch and observed green" and is explicitly "never
trusted on sight". A `full` declaration is therefore a real full gate run per phase per dispatch,
not a formality.

== THE LIVE INSTANCE (the shape the new guidance must catch) ==

Task 361's plan declared `full` at Phase 4 -- a MID-task phase -- to verify edits to one guard
script, running all 92 suites. Three details make it the canonical case:
  - the relevant suite (test-guard-destructive-git.sh) had ALREADY been run directly on the line
    above, so the full sweep added no information about the edit;
  - the plan's own text says the drift findings the full gate would produce "are expected until
    Phase 6" -- i.e. the plan knew the gate's output would be noise at that point;
  - Phase 4 and Phase 6 BOTH ran the full gate under `timeout 3000`.
A non-final phase paying the ceiling tier to produce findings the plan itself predicted and
discounted is exactly the waste this task removes.

== THE WORK ==

Make a `full` tier at a NON-FINAL phase JUSTIFY ITSELF in the plan, while the FINAL phase always
retains `full`. Apply it across the planning surface rather than in one file, because a rule written
only in plan-format.md is not read at the moment a planner assigns a tier:

  (1) context/formats/plan-format.md -- the tier definition and the tie-break. The tie-break at :271
      is the specific line that needs a cost-aware qualification: keep strict-when-uncertain for the
      FINAL phase, and require a stated reason for a non-final `full`. Settle the exact form (a
      required justification line in the phase block, versus prose guidance alone); a required field
      is checkable and prose is not, which argues for the field.
  (2) agents/planner-agent.md -- where tier assignment ACTUALLY happens, at planner-agent.md:216-227
      (step 8, which restates the strictest-when-uncertain bias at :220 and already carries the
      do-not-weaken-the-final-gate MUST NOT at :227); the plan template field at
      planner-agent.md:310-311; and the authoring checklist at planner-agent.md:384-385, which the
      file itself calls the place "where authoring-time enforcement of the tier vocabulary actually
      lives". That checklist is the enforcement point for any new required justification.
  (3) context/workflows/task-breakdown.md -- the phase template carrying the tier field at
      task-breakdown.md:76-78 and :94, plus the worked example at :131. A template that shows a bare
      tier value teaches a bare tier value.
  (4) context/contracts/phase-closure.md -- tier already participates in phase sizing at
      phase-closure.md:53 ("the one with the smallest remaining work -- fewer steps, a lower
      **Verification Tier**") and in the run-and-observe rule at :167-169. This is where a non-final
      phase's cheaper tier has to be stated as closing the phase legitimately, or implementers will
      escalate back to `full` out of caution.

== DEPENDENCY, AND WHY ==

Depends on the Gate 8 suite-selection task (366). Guidance telling a planner to pick a cheaper tier
is only actionable if a cheaper tier has something to RUN: today a `local` or `interface` tier at
Gate 8 granularity can run all 92 suites or none, because run-all.sh has no --filter/--only
(verified, zero matches). This task's guidance cites the selection flag that task introduces. Landing
the guidance first would produce plans that declare a cheap tier with no mechanism behind it.

== MUST PRESERVE ==

plan-format.md:273-277's non-negotiable invariant, verbatim in force: tiering governs GRANULARITY
ONLY, "the full gate set still runs before a phase closes and before a task completes, unchanged",
and "a tiering scheme that weakens the final gate is wrong, not a trade-off". The FINAL phase always
retains `full`. This task adds a justification requirement at non-final phases; it does not add a
cheaper option at the final one.

Also binding: ROADMAP Settled decision 15 -- Gate 8's deployed-tree coverage is knowingly reduced
under --skip-slow, so a --skip-slow pass is NOT evidence that doc-sync pins hold. The new guidance
must not let a cheaper non-final tier be read as discharging that evidence, and must not present
--skip-slow as a tier.

== SCOPE EXCLUSION, DELIBERATE AND REASONED ==

agents/reviser-agent.md is EXCLUDED, after checking. It carries no tier guidance of its own: it
defers wholly to plan-format.md at reviser-agent.md:16 ("always load"), :93 ("Follow plan-format.md
structure exactly") and :177. It therefore inherits this task's change by reference, and editing it
would add an unnecessary overlap with an open task (299) for no behavioral gain. If research finds
the revise path can reintroduce an unjustified `full` despite that deferral, record it as a
FOLLOW-UP rather than widening scope here.

== ACCEPTANCE: DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSERTED ==

  1. A real plan written under the new guidance declares a CHEAPER tier at a non-final phase, states
     its justification, and STILL PASSES ITS FINAL GATE. Demonstrated end to end on an actual task,
     not asserted in prose.
  2. The live instance above is replayed: under the new guidance, that mid-task phase selects a
     cheaper tier and the phase's edit remains genuinely covered -- show which suite covers it.
  3. A non-final `full` is still ALLOWED where warranted, and its justification requirement is
     satisfiable rather than a blocker. Show one such phase.
  4. The final phase of every plan still declares `full` and names the complete gate set per
     plan-format.md:279-282.
  5. All four surfaces agree. No surviving copy of the old unqualified tie-break in any of the four
     files, verified by grep, since a second copy is the drift mechanism.
  6. If a required justification field is chosen, the authoring checklist at planner-agent.md:384-385
     checks it, and a plan missing it is detectable.

DELIVERABLE RULE: no task-number references in deliverables outside specs/** -- cite file AND line
(the durable anchors used throughout this description), never a task number.

artifacts.summary: Research report: 01_tier-selection-discipline.md

6-phase, 4-wave implementation plan for cost-aware verification-tier selection across plan-format.md, planner-agent.md, task-breakdown.md and phase-closure.md, plus one incidental stale-label fix in plan-format-enforcement.md.
Full 6-phase implementation summary with Reasoned Exclusions evidence for Phase 6's 2 gate findings.

The plan executed as its own acceptance demonstration: 5 non-final phases declared tiers below full with stated justifications, and the final phase ran the complete gate set (33/35 green; 2 findings closed as reasoned exclusions, both traced to a pre-existing, unrelated per-session runtime-file-detection gap unconnected to any of the five edited files).

active_projects.title: Orphan sweep for deployed entries removed from the source store: the deploy adds and changes but cannot delete
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/ and lua/neotex/plugins/ai/ (never
.claude/**, a disposable deploy artifact -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md).

GOAL. The extension deploy can ADD and CHANGE but cannot DELETE. A merge-target entry removed
from the source store survives indefinitely in every already-deployed repo, because the merge
path only visits entries the fragments still provide and install-once files are never recopied.
Close that gap for hook registrations, and state the invariant where a future editor will meet it.

LIVE INSTANCE, observed 2026-10-07 in this repo's own deployed .claude/settings.json line 21:

    "command": "bash scripts/claude-ready-signal.sh 2>/dev/null || echo '{}'"

The source-store registration was deleted (root-files/settings.json is clean, verified). The
deployed copy still carries it, and no resync can remove it: the fragment merge only adds or
replaces entries it visits; install-once never recopies settings.json; and because the entry was
never in a fragment, unmerge_settings has no tracked record of it either. It is an orphan. It
invokes a script that exists nowhere, failing silently behind its own `2>/dev/null || echo '{}'`,
which is why it went unnoticed. Severity is low -- a silent no-op, not a disabled guard -- but the
CLASS is not low: the same mechanism would silently retain a registration that had become actively
wrong.

PRECEDENT TO EXTEND, not invent. merge.lua already solves exactly this shape for a different
merge target: `remove_orphaned_index_entries(index_path, valid_prefixes, context_dir)` at
merge.lua:755, documented at :746 and :689 as "cleaning orphaned entries that bypass tracked
append/remove". Hook registrations have no counterpart. Follow that function's structure and
call-siting rather than designing a new mechanism.

SCOPE:
  - An orphan sweep for hook registrations: on load/resync, remove a `.claude/hooks/*.sh` (or
    other source-store-resolvable script) registration from the target settings file when no
    loaded extension's fragment or root-files surface still provides it.
  - Reconcile the identity notion with the lint's. The hook-path lint task's research recorded a
    DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE: that lint keys fragment-coverage on any invoked script path, while
    merge.lua's hook_identity() recognizes only paths under `hooks/`. The divergence was accepted
    in that task's scope, not resolved. Resolve it here, in ONE place both consume, so a later
    reader cannot find two different answers to "is this the same registration".
  - MUST NOT remove a hand-written hook. The existing custom-hook carve-out (a command not
    recognizable as a source-store hook invocation is never matched, moved or deduped) governs the
    sweep too: an unrecognized command is left strictly alone, never swept as an orphan. This is
    the single most dangerous possible regression in this task -- a sweep that over-reaches
    silently deletes a user's own hook registration.
  - State the invariant in the source-store/deploy-boundary documentation: the deploy adds and
    changes but does not delete, which merge targets now sweep orphans and which do not, and the
    by-hand repair for a deploy predating a sweep (`rm .claude/settings.json` then reload --
    install-once copies fresh only when the target is ABSENT; `deploy-headless.sh --wipe` restores
    its own snapshot as the merge base and reintroduces the staleness).

REGRESSION SAFETY is a first-class requirement, not a closing check:
  - Measure the affected deploys BEFORE and AFTER: registration count, per-event duplicate count,
    and that `env` and `permissions` survive byte-identical. A settings file is not "fine" because
    it parses.
  - Verify against a REAL stale deploy, never only a synthetic fixture. A fixture reconstructed
    from memory cannot carry the shapes a field file actually has.
  - Anchor detection on the `"command"` JSON key, not a text grep. A naive `.claude/hooks/` grep
    matches root-files/settings.json's own `_comment` field -- a false-positive hazard already
    found by the lint task's research.
  - Run the pre-existing extension/merge specs, not only new ones, and treat a newly red
    pre-existing test as a regression this task caused.

NON-GOALS (owned elsewhere; do not absorb, and do not edit their files):
  - Script and test corpus duplication, dead code and slow tests -- the standing probe-consumer
    task owns these as one systemic item, per the settled decision that a systemic cost is filed
    once against a probe's output rather than as a stream of point defects.
  - Context-corpus reachability and dead/overlapping context files -- owned by the reachability
    probe task.
  - Neovim repo hygiene (stale init.lua.backup, project-overview.md regeneration, README link) --
    owned by the repo-hygiene task.
  - Task support files tracked-or-ignored -- owned by the support-file sweep task.
  - Missing `desc` fields on keymap.set calls -- owned by the keymap documentation task.
  Removal propagation is this task's only subject; the generic word "cruft" must not be used to
  pull any of the above in.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  1. A registration present in the deployed target but provided by no loaded extension's fragment
     or root-files surface is removed by an ordinary load/resync, demonstrated against the live
     line-21 instance above (or a faithful copy of that file if it has since been repaired).
  2. A hand-written hook command not recognizable as a source-store hook invocation survives a
     sweep untouched, with a dedicated regression test.
  3. The identity notion is defined in exactly one place, consumed by both the sweep and the
     hook-path lint; a test asserts the two agree on a path outside `hooks/`.
  4. Before/after measurements are reported for every affected deploy: registration count, zero
     per-event duplicates, and `env`/`permissions` byte-identical.
  5. The pre-existing extension/merge specs still pass; any newly red pre-existing test is treated
     as caused by this task.
  6. The source-store/deploy-boundary documentation states the add/change-but-not-delete invariant,
     names which merge targets sweep orphans, and records the by-hand repair for an older deploy.

active_projects.title: Make the required .orchestrator-handoff.json schema reach the dispatched agent
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree
-- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No
task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/**
(rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md); they are permitted in this description and elsewhere
in specs/**.

GOAL. Make the .orchestrator-handoff.json schema that validate-handoff.sh enforces reach the
dispatched agent BEFORE it writes the handoff, so a missing required field stops being discovered
only by the validator failing after the phase's work is already done and committed.

MEASURED INCIDENT (do not re-derive; re-confirm only). 2026-10-08, /orchestrate 742,735 --hard
--lit --fable in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic, session sess_1791448118_c50a56. On dispatch_seq 3 (task
742, implement phase 1 of 10) a lean-implementation-hard-agent completed the phase GREEN -- the
module landed, scoped and full library builds green, 0 sorries, axiom count at baseline, two
commits -- and then wrote .orchestrator-handoff.json WITHOUT the required `artifacts` array.
validate-handoff.sh scored it 12 PASS / 1 FAIL ("Required field missing or not an array:
artifacts"). orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh returned verdict=defer, performed NO state.json
transition, and queued defect_class=HANDOFF_VALIDATION_FAILED attributed to
core/skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, detecting_site
skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md:cycle-postflight-handoff-validation. The work was preserved, but the
cycle still consumed one of that task's 13 hard-mode work cycles for a bookkeeping miss rather than
a work failure.

WHY THE WORKAROUND IS THE EVIDENCE, NOT THE FIX. The orchestrator then hand-injected the
requirement into the prompt of every subsequent dispatch ("your handoff MUST include a non-empty
`artifacts` array of {type, path} entries alongside
status/phases_completed/phases_total/blockers/summary/dispatch_seq"). All 15 later handoffs across
both tasks passed, including 14/14 and 12/0/0 validator runs. So the requirement is learnable and
sufficient the moment the agent is told -- the defect is that nothing in the dispatch path tells
it, and a per-run prompt injection by one orchestrator is not durable.

GOAL. Teach core/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh the stage-based specs/ROADMAP.md layout so
--regenerate works on it and round-trips without content loss, fix the script's silent abort, and
make its destructive-overwrite refusal a permanent property.

=== USER RULING, settled 2026-10-08, DO NOT RE-LITIGATE ===
The roadmap SHOULD BE GENERATED. The generated-artifact premise established by #306 stands and is
authoritative. The generator must be extended to emit and round-trip the stage-based layout.
Do NOT retire, narrow, or disable --regenerate, and do NOT drop the conclusion stage's Step 5
call -- both alternatives were considered and rejected by the user in favour of teaching the
generator.

=== EVIDENCE (measured; re-confirm only, do not re-derive) ===
Found live during an `/orchestrate 739,740 --lit --fable` run in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic,
2026-10-08.

`core/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate` aborts with exit 1 and ZERO stderr output.
Reproduce: `bash .claude/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate` in BimodalLogic at commit
79f3fe7cc.

Root cause, traced with `bash -x`: the script assumes a fixed section vocabulary -- `## Goal`,
`## Gate state`, `## Next`, `## Open work`, `## Checks before and after every call`,
`## Settled decisions (do not re-litigate)`, `## Standing rules`,
`## Unfiled observations (none worth a task yet)` -- assembled by `assemble_roadmap()` near
line 393. BimodalLogic's specs/ROADMAP.md was restructured by its own commit 5e28ad981
("roadmap: trim to essentials, restructure by stage with per-batch rationale") into a
stage-based layout whose actual headers are: `## Run order at a glance`,
`## Stage 0 -- User rulings and marker corrections`,
`## Stage 1 -- Decidability of L+ (preempts everything)`,
`## Stage 2 -- Supporting semantics and metalogic`,
`## Stage 3 -- Datasets, examples and documentation`,
`## Stage 4 -- The long fronts (low priority)`, `## Not scoped as tasks`, `## Maintenance`,
`## Related`. NONE of the expected headers exist. So every `extract_section()` returns empty,
`authored_next` is empty, and `covered_ids_from()` (lines 382-386) runs
`grep -E '^/orchestrate ' <<<""`, which exits 1 on no-match; under the script's own
`set -euo pipefail` (line 28) that status propagates through the command substitution and kills
the script.

=== THREE SUB-FAULTS, ALL OWED ===
1. THE SILENT DEATH. The script's own header (lines 24-26) promises: "Every invocation, every
   mode, prints one always-present machine-readable stderr marker:
   `<!-- roadmap-generation mode=M tasks=N topics=T runs=R pruned=P retained=A -->`. This never
   affects the exit code -- it is a diagnostic, not a failure signal." That marker did NOT
   appear. The failure is undiagnosable without `bash -x`. Make the promise true, including on
   the error paths.
2. THE UNGUARDED grep-IN-PIPELINE-UNDER-pipefail PATTERN. In `covered_ids_from()`, no-match is a
   NORMAL condition, not an error. Audit the whole script for the same shape rather than
   patching only this one call site.
3. THE OVERWRITE NEAR-MISS -- the more dangerous half. Had the regenerate SUCCEEDED it would
   have silently overwritten the hand-authored stage structure with its own fixed template,
   destroying content. Even with the generator taught the new layout, it must detect a roadmap
   whose section vocabulary it does not recognise and refuse LOUDLY with a named reason rather
   than proceeding to emit. Treat destructive-overwrite refusal as a PERMANENT property, not a
   transitional guard.

=== WHAT IS OWED ===
--regenerate works on the stage-based layout, round-trips without content loss, emits the
promised stderr marker on every invocation and every mode including failures, refuses loudly on
an unrecognised vocabulary, and has no remaining no-match-as-error pipeline. The generation
contract core/context/formats/roadmap-format.md must be updated to describe the stage-based
layout it now emits -- a generator and a format spec that disagree is the precondition that
produced this defect.

=== VERIFY AGAINST THE REAL FILE ===
BimodalLogic's specs/ROADMAP.md at commit 79f3fe7cc (or later) is the regression fixture: a
successful --regenerate against it must preserve its Stage 0-4 structure, its per-batch rationale
prose, and its hand-authored `/orchestrate ...` batch lines. Check also whether --prune has the
same vocabulary assumption; it shares `extract_section()`. Note --print claims it never reads an
existing ROADMAP.md, so it may be unaffected -- CONFIRM rather than assume.

ALSO CHECK. core/scripts/deprecated/roadmap-integration.sh exists beside the live one -- confirm
no caller resolves the deprecated copy.

=== IMPACT ===
The conclusion stage's Step 5 is a silent no-op on every /orchestrate invocation in BimodalLogic
and no specs/ROADMAP.md commit is produced. Not urgent -- that roadmap is hand-maintained and
currently accurate -- but it is a live, reproducible, silent no-op in a stage that claims to run
exactly once per invocation, and the overwrite near-miss makes a naive fix actively risky.

=== BACKLOG RECONCILIATION (already checked; do NOT duplicate, re-scope, or fold into) ===
- #306 [completed] roadmap_generated_artifact -- the record that MADE specs/ROADMAP.md a
  generated artifact with context/formats/roadmap-format.md as its generation contract. Terminal.
- #313 [not_started] advisory_lint_for_roadmap_batch_proposals -- adjacent but a DIFFERENT
  mechanism (authoring-time lint over hand-typed batch prose comparing file_scope). Not a home
  for a generator crash.
- #273 [completed] three_channel_orchestration_conclusion_stage -- built the conclusion stage
  whose Step 5/Step 6 are defective here.
- BimodalLogic's own 61-record list was also checked: nothing covers roadmap-integration.sh.

=== NOT IN SCOPE ===
The caller-split documentation and the missing conclusion report block are the sibling record's
territory (#372). No change to /orchestrate's conclusion-stage contract beyond what the
generator's own behaviour forces. --prune behaviour changes only if the shared
`extract_section()` fix touches it.

=== FILE SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT ===
core/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh and core/context/formats/roadmap-format.md at minimum, but
the full set depends on whether --prune and --print turn out to be affected. SET file_scope AT
PLAN TIME, after checking those two modes. An absent scope makes this record invisible to the

active_projects.title: Issue-log entries with a null resolution are permanently invisible to the conclusion stage that exists to act on them
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree
-- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No
task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/**
(rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md); they are permitted in this description and elsewhere
in specs/**.

GOAL. Decide and document what a null `resolution` means on a `kind: "issue"` entry in
`issues.jsonl`. Today it means "silently unreachable by the only consumer built to act on it",
and no contract says so.

=== WHY THIS EXISTS ===
Found live during an `/orchestrate 739,740 --lit --fable` run in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic on
2026-10-08. The conclusion stage (Move 5) reported all three channels empty and derived zero
proposals. That was mechanically correct and substantively wrong: six `kind: "issue"` entries
recording real friction were structurally unable to reach it.

=== THE MECHANISM (both halves read and verified 2026-10-08) ===
- core/scripts/issue-record.sh: `--resolution` is OPTIONAL. Its own usage block lists the required
  fields as --kind, --class, --severity, --what-happened plus exactly one task-resolution form;
  --resolution is not among them. Validation at line ~190 is guarded by `if [ -n "$resolution_arg" ]`,
  so an omitted flag is never checked. Line ~387 then writes an explicit JSON null:
  `resolution: (if $resolution == "" then null else $resolution end)`.
- core/context/formats/issue-log.md line ~94 declares `resolution` as `no (nullable)` with a closed
  three-value set `fixed_inline | worked_around | open`. A null is therefore SCHEMA-LEGAL. The
  row's notes column is EMPTY -- the schema never says what a null means.
- core/scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh line ~253 filters:
  `map(select(.kind != "win" and ((.resolution // "") as $r | $r == "open" or $r == "worked_around")))`
  A null coerces to "", which matches neither arm, so the entry is dropped.
- core/context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md's "The Filter Predicate" section (lines ~50-59) states
  the intent: an entry "enters classification only when its `resolution` field is `open` or
  `worked_around`", and an entry with `fixed_inline` "is already closed and generates no channel
  item -- nothing remains to propose." NULL IS UNADDRESSED BY THAT PROSE ENTIRELY -- neither
  declared closed nor admitted. That silence is the root defect, independent of which code path
  changes.

=== THE RESULT ===
Omitting one optional flag silently makes a recorded issue permanently unreachable by the only
consumer built to act on it. There is no warning at write time, no tally at read time, and no
mention in the report -- the stage renders "zero proposals" indistinguishably from "nothing was
wrong".

=== EVIDENCE FROM THE ORIGINATING RUN (regression fixture; entry ids verified against the files) ===
Six `kind: "issue"` entries, all `resolution: null`, all dropped:
- specs/739_e2_depth_two_stratification_shared_stratum_falsifier/issues.jsonl -- three
  `class: "tooling"` entries and one `class: "proof-repair"`: iss_1791491569197_zKdUqQ,
  iss_1791491985760_3vcrAx, iss_1791492027880_W6tDkM, iss_1791493419356_KeoHGd. The dispatch's own
  report described four real toolchain pitfalls hit and fixed (hand-built Fintype, Int.leInduction,
  decide'd neighbour tables, omega inside anonymous constructors).
- specs/740_ktype_summary_finite_preds_restatement/issues.jsonl -- two `class: "gate-collision"`
  entries: iss_1791494232271_nNKsBs and iss_1791494859307_glbAlq. These are the pre-commit
  typst-sync gate forcing per-file commits into one phase commit, and the harness INV group going
  red because line-count changes aged two generated inventory blocks.
  NOTE: iss_1791495145946_fTTfhl in that same file is NOT an instance of this defect -- it is
  `kind: "win"`, `class: "time-saved"`, `resolution: null`, and the filter exempts wins in the
  opposite direction. Do not cite it as evidence.
These are precisely the recurring cross-task friction the stage's own Cross-Task Grouping Rule
exists to surface: two `gate-collision` entries in one task, and a `tooling` class appearing three
times, would have grouped into proposals had they been reachable.

=== WHAT IS OWED -- PICK ONE PRIMARY REMEDY AND RECORD WHY (do not do all three blindly) ===
1. TIGHTEN THE WRITER. Make --resolution required for `kind: "issue"`, leaving it optional for
   `kind: "win"` (which the filter exempts anyway). Catches the omission while the author still
   knows the answer. Costs a breaking change to every existing issue-record.sh call site that
   omits it -- ENUMERATE THOSE FIRST before committing to this option.
2. WIDEN THE READER. Treat null as `open` in the aggregator's filter. Zero writer churn and
   recovers the six already-written entries, but silently reclassifies entries whose authors may
   have meant "not worth acting on", and arguably makes the closed enum's third value redundant.
3. SURFACE THE GAP. Keep both halves as-is but have the aggregator count null-resolution issue
   entries and the stage report them as a named tally beside the unknown-class tally, so they are
   visible even when unactionable.
Options 2 and 3 compose; 1 and 2 are substitutes. WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, both issue-log.md's
`resolution` row and conclusion-stage.md's "The Filter Predicate" section MUST be updated to state
explicitly what a null means.

=== SUB-QUESTIONS ALREADY ANSWERED DURING TASK CREATION (do not re-litigate; verify if changing) ===
- `suggested_channel` does NOT have the same shape, and is benign. It is null on every entry in
  both fixture files, but the aggregator already handles that explicitly at line ~262:
  `suggested_channel_hints: (map(.suggested_channel) | map(select(. != null)) | unique)`. Nulls are
  filtered out of the hint list rather than silently breaking a predicate. Combined with the
  Hint-Versus-Decision Rule (nothing reads it to act automatically), no fix is owed here.
- THE AGGREGATOR IS THE SOLE CONSUMER of issues.jsonl. Both other candidate readers explicitly
  forbid themselves from reading it: core/skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md ("Do NOT wire this harvest to
  `issues.jsonl` as a replacement -- surfacing that log is explicitly out of scope here and belongs
  exclusively to the separate orchestration conclusion stage") and memory/skills/skill-learn/SKILL.md
  (same prohibition verbatim in substance). /distill's telemetry sub-modes do not read it -- a grep
  for `issues.jsonl` across agent-system/extensions/ returns no hit in skill-distill. Therefore a
  filter change has NO blast radius outside the conclusion stage. Re-verify with that same grep
  before relying on this.

=== NOT IN SCOPE ===
No change to the three-channel derivation contract, the per-channel approval gates, or the approval
ledger. No change to the `kind: "win"` exemption, which is correct as written. No retroactive edit
to already-written issues.jsonl entries in any repo -- this is append-only capture (see the Review
Happens Only At This Stage boundary); if option 2 is chosen the six entries above become reachable
automatically, which is the point. Do not fold in the defects tracked by the roadmap-generator or
conclusion-report-block tasks filed alongside this one.

=== BACKLOG RECONCILIATION (already checked; do NOT duplicate or fold into) ===
- #273 [completed] three_channel_orchestration_conclusion_stage -- built the conclusion stage whose
  filter is the consumer half of this defect. Terminal.
- #371 [not_started] roadmap_generator_stage_layout_and_silent_abort and #372 [not_started]
  conclusion_stage_report_block_and_caller_split -- filed in the same session for DIFFERENT
  conclusion-stage defects. This is a third, independent defect: no dependencies[] edge is declared
  on either, and it must not be merged into them.
- A keyword sweep of the global list (issue.log|issues\.jsonl|issue-record|resolution) found no
  covering task. BimodalLogic's own list covers nothing here either.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- A null `resolution` on a `kind: "issue"` entry either cannot be written, or is reachable by the
  conclusion stage, or is explicitly counted and reported.
- In ALL THREE cases, both issue-log.md and conclusion-stage.md state what null means rather than
  leaving it undefined.
- Regression fixture: a re-run of orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate over tasks 739
  and 740 in ~/Projects/BimodalLogic must no longer silently return zero proposals while six issue
  entries sit unreachable.

=== FILE SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT ===
core/scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh, core/scripts/issue-record.sh,
core/context/formats/issue-log.md, core/context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md -- the exact subset
depends on which remedy is chosen. SET file_scope AT PLAN TIME. An absent scope makes this record
invisible to the batch admission gate's overlap detection -- a known blindness, not an exemption.

active_projects.description:
RELOCATED 2026-10-08 from ~/Projects/Logos/Verification (task 252 there) after its research phase. The evidence commits fc9f786e and 96986be6, the incident record specs/224_review_and_refactor_fragile_gate_infrastructure/issues.jsonl, and typst/manual/generated/components/zigzag.typ all live in that repository, not this one. The deliverables live here, under agent-system/extensions/core/; redeploy afterwards via deploy-headless.sh.

Diagnose and fix the silent staging drop in git-commit-scoped.sh

--- WHY ---

Every dispatch in the agent system commits through
`agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh`. During the pre-tag gate-infrastructure
audit, that script silently omitted a file it was explicitly told to stage, gave no diagnostic, and
exited successfully.

--- EVIDENCE (measured 2026-10-08, recorded at `costly` severity) ---

A phase regenerating ten Typst fragments listed all ten in its `stage_paths` and invoked
`git-commit-scoped.sh` once. The resulting commit `fc9f786e` carried nine of them. The tenth,
`typst/manual/generated/components/zigzag.typ`, was omitted: HEAD kept a stale snapshot inherited
from a much older historical commit (certificate identity `e7376e62...`, `FramedChannel.CodecModel`
naming) while the working tree held the correct regeneration (identity `3591ddc8...`,
`Interface.CodecModel` naming).

Three facts make this worse than a one-off:

1. The script exited 0 and printed nothing about the omission. A caller cannot distinguish "staged
   ten, committed ten" from "staged ten, committed nine" from the exit code or the output.
2. The phase's own verification did not catch it, because it checked exit codes and ran the
   sync-check against the WORKING TREE, which was correct. Only a post-commit `git diff` against
   HEAD would have shown it, and nothing in the contract asks for one.
3. A fresh clone's disk state equals HEAD, so the gate that same effort had just promoted to
   blocking (`typst-manual-sync-check.sh` via `.github/workflows/docs.yml`) would have failed on
   the next fresh checkout. It was found only by a routine `git status` sweep at wrap-up, after the
   summary and a downstream task's description had already been written, and patched by a follow-up
   commit `96986be6`.

The root cause was NOT determined at the time and is this task's first obligation. Candidate
mechanisms worth ruling on rather than assuming: the ephemeral-runtime-file `:(exclude)` injection
loop silently matching a path it should not; the `specs/.commit-lock/` mutex or the
`claim-acquire`/`claim-release` contended-path lease dropping an entry; a `git add` pathspec
interaction with `.gitignore` via `git check-ignore`; or a concurrent writer's index interaction,
since the repository was under genuine multi-agent use in that window.

--- SCOPE ---

(1) Reproduce the omission, or establish with evidence why it cannot be reproduced and what that
    rules out. A non-reproduction is an acceptable Phase 1 outcome only if it narrows the cause.
(2) Rule on the mechanism, with the ruling grounded in the script's own code rather than inference
    from the symptom.
(3) Make the failure loud. Whatever the cause, a positive pathspec the caller named and the commit
    did not carry must produce a non-zero exit or a clearly-marked diagnostic. A caller must not be
    able to receive exit 0 for a partial commit.
(4) Add a fixture that fails without the fix and passes with it, in the script's own test suite.

--- OUT OF SCOPE ---

Widening the staging contract, relaxing the over-staging prohibitions in `rules/git-workflow.md`, or
any change that makes callers stage more broadly to work around the defect. The fix is a correct
narrow commit plus a loud failure, never a wider pathspec.

--- FILE SCOPE ---

The deliverables live in the agent-system source store outside this repository (resolve via
`.claude-extensions.json`'s `source_dir`; the store is at `~/.config/nvim/agent-system`). Never
hand-edit under `.claude/`, which a deploy regenerates. `file_scope` is empty by design, as it is
for the other agent-system tasks.

--- ACCEPTANCE ---

A recorded ruling on the mechanism with its evidence; the script exits non-zero or emits a marked
diagnostic whenever a named positive pathspec is not carried by the resulting commit; a fixture that
fails without the change and passes with it; and the deployed trees refreshed so the fix is the
version dispatches actually run.

artifacts.summary: Rules out three of four candidate mechanisms for the git-commit-scoped.sh silent staging drop (ephemeral-exclude injection, --task contention-claim lease, gitignore interaction); reproduces the exact symptom under a forced specs/.commit-lock mutex fail-open plus a concurrent second writer naming the same path; recommends a mechanism-agnostic post-commit integrity gate as the loud-failure fix and a deterministic two-writer fixture.

5-phase, 6-hour plan: red fixture, V8 intent-snapshot/post-commit integrity gate with exit code 5, false-positive dimension tests, documentation of the ruling and git semantics, deploy plus full gate set.
Implementation summary for the V8 silent-staging-drop fix across all 5 phases.

active_projects.title: Verify phase commits carry every file the phase touched
active_projects.description:
SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree; see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). REDEPLOY AFTERWARDS via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md).

=== WHY ===

The "silent staging drop" that task 374 was opened for was a CALLER omission, not a git-commit-scoped.sh defect. In ~/Projects/Logos/Verification, task 224 phase 5 regenerated ten typst/manual/generated/components/*.typ fragments. Its commit command hand-typed a stage_paths list naming only nine of them. zigzag.typ was never passed to the script. The script committed exactly what it was given and exited 0. HEAD kept a stale zigzag.typ until a manual follow-up commit (96986be6).

=== EVIDENCE (verified 2026-10-09 by reading the original transcript) ===

- Transcript: ~/.claude/projects/-home-benjamin-Projects-Logos-Verification/95371aec-e4b8-4b00-8973-dc67fe59acd6/subagents/agent-a6a393c380d25ea8b.jsonl, tool_use toolu_01JgkBy3RifdvaRCCs4DZDtt at 2026-10-08T21:28:54Z. Its stage_paths names channel, crc8, receiver, ring_buffer, seq_num, stuff, stuffed_channel, varint and vec_queue, but NOT zigzag.
- The phase's own progress file, specs/224_review_and_refactor_fragile_gate_infrastructure/progress/phase-5-progress.json (committed in fc9f786e), DOES list zigzag.typ in objective 2's files_touched. The omission was mechanically detectable from data the phase already recorded.
- The command piped the script's output through '| tail -25', so the caller could not observe the script's exit code at all.
- The same call passed --task 224, contradicting task 374's research claim that phase commits never pass --task.
- The incident record (Verification specs/224_.../issues.jsonl, entry iss_1791495993077_nD5IuJ) wrongly states the path WAS listed. Task 374's research and plan inherited that false premise.
- Task 374's script-side integrity gate (new exit code 5) compares only NAMED paths against HEAD. It would NOT have caught this incident, because the missing path was never named.

=== SCOPE ===

1. POST-COMMIT COMPLETENESS CHECK. After a phase commit, every path in that phase's progress files_touched must be clean against HEAD (git status --porcelain -- <paths> is empty). Otherwise fail loudly, naming each dirty path. Research decides the enforcement site: the implementation agent's phase-commit template, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, or the phase-closure contract. Prefer a mechanical site (a script) over prose instructions.

2. DERIVE THE STAGE LIST. Build the phase-commit pathspec from files_touched plus the task directory, instead of hand-typing it. This removes the omission at its source.

3. EXPOSE THE EXIT CODE. Remove '| tail' piping from every documented phase-commit invocation template, or require set -o pipefail, so callers observe git-commit-scoped.sh's real exit code. Without this, task 374's new exit code 5 never reaches a caller. Enumerate every template and doc that shows the piped form.

4. CORRECT THE RECORD. APPEND (never edit; issues.jsonl is append-only) a correcting entry to Verification's specs/224_review_and_refactor_fragile_gate_infrastructure/issues.jsonl, citing the transcript evidence above. Ensure task 374's recorded ruling does not state the disproven cause (a concurrency race, or a dropped named pathspec). Check 374's state at implementation time: it may already record UNDETERMINED or the corrected mechanism.

=== OUT OF SCOPE ===

- Whether specs/.commit-lock should fail closed. Task 374's plan already flags this as a separate follow-up.
- Any change to git-commit-scoped.sh's staging semantics.
- Widening any pathspec beyond files_touched plus the task directory.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

- A fixture where a phase touches N files but the commit names N-1 fails loudly, naming the missing path.
- The documented phase-commit template exposes the script's real exit code.
- Verification's task 224 issues.jsonl carries an appended correcting entry citing the transcript.
- Deployed trees are refreshed so dispatches run the new check.

=== BACKLOG RECONCILIATION (already checked) ===

Tasks 302 (scoped_commit_directory_pathspec_and_task_lease), 304 (out_of_repo_pathspec_aborts_whole_commit) and 318 (wire_directory_pathspec_lint_as_verify_deploy_gate) target different pathspec defects inside the script, not caller-side completeness. Do not fold into them.
